## Context / Problem
`tests/unit/test_audit_serve.py::test_serve_binds_loopback_ephemeral_and_lists_ticket` fails with `TimeoutError: timed out` on its `urllib.request.urlopen(..., timeout=5)` during loaded full `make verify` runs (fix-chihuahua at 4f8cd749a61; fix-jaeger at d413a0497e5, load average 33 on 18 cores), while passing in isolation (5/5 on the branch, 3/3 on origin/main). Closed bug ignitable-noteworthy-osprey was a different failure (network guard leak), so this is a separate cause.

## Root cause (measured)
The 5 s read bound covers the whole `GET /` render, and that render spawns git child processes whose cost scales with host load, not with the HTTP contract:
- `create_app`'s index (`src/rebar/audit/server.py` `_audited_tickets`) calls `rebar.list_tickets` then `audit_trail` per ticket (`src/rebar/audit/read.py:205-217`).
- Every one of those reads runs `ensure_fresh` (`src/rebar/_engine_support/reads.py:192`), which spawns `git rev-parse --verify <branch>` at line 221 before the 60 s marker throttle, and on the first read a `git fetch` via `_store/sync.py` `_coordinated_fetch`.
- Profiled with one audited ticket: 6 git processes on the first render (fetch + 5 rev-parse), 5 on a throttled render; 0.2-0.45 s unloaded.
- Deterministic reproduction: a PATH shim `git` that sleeps 0.8 s before exec'ing the real git makes the unchanged test fail with the same `TimeoutError` every run (1 failed in 68 s); with 0 s delay it passes.
Classification: TEST bug. The work in the request is the store's uniform read policy, so the test's tight wall-clock bound measures host subprocess cost. The suite's designated hang guard is pytest-timeout (`pyproject.toml` `timeout = 300`, `timeout_method = "thread"`, documented as sized to dwarf legitimate cost). The 10 s `uv.started` deadline has the same flaw for server startup. Precedent: Gerrit 3297 (30f06afc412) replaced a wall-clock bound with an ordering check plus a mutant check.
The probe-before-throttle cost at `reads.py:221` (1 + 4N git spawns per index render even when throttled) is a real but separate production inefficiency; it is filed as its own bug linked discovered_from this one and is out of scope here.

## Approach
Make the test measure the contract (binds 127.0.0.1 on the requested ephemeral port, answers 200, lists the seeded ticket) instead of elapsed time:
1. Readiness by state, not deadline: a helper waits until `uv.started` is true or the server thread has exited. uvicorn 0.52.1 calls `sys.exit(STARTUP_FAILURE)` on a bind `OSError` (`uvicorn/server.py:183`), which ends the thread before `started` is set (`server.py:196`), so a bind failure is reported at once with no deadline.
2. Assert the bind directly from the listening sockets (`uv.servers[*].sockets[*].getsockname()` == `("127.0.0.1", port)`).
3. Issue the request with no client-side read deadline; a genuine hang is bounded by the suite's 300 s pytest-timeout budget, the documented hang guard.
4. Companion mutant check (precedent 3297 style): start the server on a port already held by another socket and assert the readiness helper reports "thread exited without starting" promptly instead of waiting, proving the state-based wait still catches the real failure.
No production code changes; no autouse fixtures added; no new child processes (if any are needed they go through `tests/_subprocess_env.subprocess_env`).

## Scope
- `tests/unit/test_audit_serve.py` — readiness helper, bind assertion, unbounded read, companion bind-failure test.

## Testing
- Failing first: under the slow-git PATH shim (0.8 s per git call) the current test fails with `TimeoutError`; after the change the same command passes.
- Companion test: a pre-bound port makes the readiness helper return "not started" with the thread dead.
- Unloaded: `pytest -n0 tests/unit/test_audit_serve.py` passes; `tests/unit -k audit` passes.
- `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass with the worktree `.venv/bin` first on PATH.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Root cause identified with a deterministic reproduction (for example a throttled server thread) before any fix.
- [ ] The test passes under that reproduction.
- [ ] `test_serve_binds_loopback_ephemeral_and_lists_ticket` contains no wall-clock deadline on server startup or on the HTTP read; it asserts the listening socket is `127.0.0.1:<port>`.
- [ ] A companion test starts the server on an occupied port and asserts the readiness helper reports failure with the server thread exited; it passes.
- [ ] `pytest -n0 tests/unit/test_audit_serve.py` and `pytest tests/unit -k audit` pass; `make lint` and `make typecheck` exit 0.
- [ ] The probe-before-throttle inefficiency is filed as a bug linked discovered_from this ticket.
